prompt: Run the performance tests for firmware 2.1.0.

text: Firmware 2.1.0 adds an EasyMesh agent (`mesh-agent`, enabled by default) and a cloud telemetry service, and updates odhcpd [[ev:TB-01/doc/docs/firmware/2.1.0.md#new-features]]. For a performance pass I suggest three tests. I added the 12-hour endurance test because a new resident process is the most likely source of memory or stability regressions; on the 2.0.4 nightly runs it was stable.

args.title: Performance tests · fw 2.1.0
args.rationale: Performance suite plus a stability check for the new resident process.

items.rationale: Baseline throughput check, required for every release candidate.
Resolver latency belongs to the performance suite; the resolver path is unchanged in 2.1.0.
New mesh-agent process in 2.1.0 → stability and memory risk over a 12 h soak.

text: Plan {{plan_id}} is approved. Starting the run on the testbench.

Run finished on RTR-AX3000 · fw {{fw}} ({{report_id}}): **1 passed, 2 failed.**

| Test | Verdict | Measured | Threshold |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-PERF-003 TCP throughput | FAIL | 845.0 Mbps avg · 3.80 % retransmissions | avg ≥ 900 Mbps · ≤ 1.0 % |
| TC-DNS-005 DNS latency | PASS | p95 46.03 ms | p95 ≤ 50 ms |
| TC-END-004 Endurance 12 h | FAIL | OOM at 9 h 40 m · throughput floor 611.5 Mbps | no crash · min ≥ 800 Mbps |

- **TC-PERF-003:** throughput fell to 0 for about 2 s at 21:00:14 [[ev:{{test_run:TC-PERF-003}}/metric/throughput_mbps/1791406814]], exactly when the lab switch logged `GigabitEthernet1/0/7` going down [[ev:{{test_run:TC-PERF-003}}/log/switch-syslog/7]]. The DUT log is clean in that window, so this may be a lab issue rather than the firmware.
- **TC-END-004:** the kernel OOM killer stopped `mesh-agent` (PID 1201) after 9 h 40 m [[ev:{{test_run:TC-END-004}}/log/dut-syslog/222]], after free memory had fallen steadily [[ev:{{test_run:TC-END-004}}/check/mem_trend]].

Do you want me to analyse the root cause of the failures?
